page.layout: One page of text in a single column; margin notes at the right giving section numbers in Roman numerals (LXVII to LXXII). Running head at the top; catchword-like signature "i 4" at the foot is a gathering mark.

main_text.p: astro obuersa: eoq; ortus caniculæ signo incolas vti. Enimuerò Aristoteles, præ ter callidlittle, quâ animalia in vita sua degenda vsurpant, descriptionem, etiam huiusmodi quædam narrat, vt qui per- multum diligentię plerisq; eorum impę derit: & non obiter, sed serio narrationi- bus hisce vacauerit: ad summam LXX circiter libros de ijs composuit, conatús que est longiore quàm historia requirit narratione singula tractare. nosq; insti- tuimus, ea quæ rarum aliquid habent, aut mirabile, cùm ex ijs, tum ex alijs deli bare. Aitigitur, terrestria omnia re LXVII. spirare, quæcunq; pulmones habent: ve spas autem & apes non respirare.

Item, quibus venter, ijs etiam vesicâ esse: LXVIII. ac contrà. Exsanguia esse cùm alia LXIX. multa animalia, tû in vniuersum quę plu res quatuor habér pedes. Omnia cri LXX. nita viuos edere fœtus: nô vicissim. O- LXXI. mnia animalia inferiorem mouere man- dibulam: demto fluuiatili crocodilo, qui solus superiore mouet. Esse inIllyrio LXXII. & Pânonia monychos. Nullû animal in- uentû esse, quod solidâ vngulá & duo ha beret cornua: asinû Indicû solida vngula et vno esse cornu. solûq; de solidungulis talum

page.notes: Margin references LXVII–LXXII are placed at the right beside their lines; the printed marks are shown at approximate positions. Several words are doubtful due to print quality, notably "callidi-tatis" (read as "callid">little") and "conatús"; the line "talum" at the foot is a catchword-like continuation and the printed Roman numerals are inferred. Page furniture: the signature "i 4" is at the foot.
